summary: Status checks on 24 programmes in the Americas and Europe using official sources only. Set active from current official pages: eight Panama investor categories (SNM's current requirement sheets, plus Decreto Ejecutivo 199 of 2021 which raised the forestry minimums), Curaçao's investor permit (page updated Sept 2026, amounts now in XCG), Turks and Caicos Home Owner's Permit (Border Control site and FAQ) and Ukraine's investor immigration route (current law; yearly quota dropped from 20 Oct 2023). Set closed: Prince Edward Island's investor streams (100% and Partial Ownership closed after 20 Sept 2018, from archived PEI pages that also give the C$150,000/C$600,000/C$200,000 escrow rules). Austria gained the 1973 and 1985 provision dates (launched left empty per decision 14). Several sites (Mexico, Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Légifrance, Cyprus Audit Office) blocked automated access, so those statuses and most missing start dates stay open.

events.title: Constitutional provision names economic achievements as grounds for naturalisation in the interest of the Republic
events.description: The Citizenship Act amendment BGBl. Nr. 394/1973 (Art. I Z 5) gave the constitutional provision its wording: residence and other requirements are waived when the federal government confirms that the person's past or expected extraordinary achievements, in particular in scientific, economic, artistic or sporting fields, are in the interest of the Republic. Known from the RIS note on the 1985 text; the 1973 amendment itself was not read, so only the year is recorded.
events.quote: insbesondere auf wissenschaftlichen, wirtschaftlichen, künstlerischen oder sportlichen Gebieten, im Interesse der Republik liegt. ( BGBl. Nr. 394/1973 , Art. I Z 5) (Verfassungsbestimmung)

events.title: Ukraine drops the yearly immigration quota except in case of mass arrival

The last yearly quota order found is for 2023, and the 2022 and 2023 orders put no limit on the investor category.

programs.notes: Not an advertised investment programme and no published price. A constitutional provision lets a Land grant citizenship without 10 years' residence, proof of income or renunciation of the old nationality when the federal government confirms that the person's past and expected 'extraordinary achievements' are in the special interest of the Republic. Used for scientists, artists, athletes and business people alike; official statistics do not split by field. Procedure regulated by BGBl. II 39/2014. Names and professions of confirmed persons are published (at least since 2016-2017). Statistik Austria counts 10 to 54 naturalisations a year in 2007-2023. The European Commission (COM(2019) 12, p. 4, fn. 10) lists Austria among states whose law equates national interest with economic interest. The provision has existed since the Citizenship Act 1965 (ministry statement 8483/AB). Its wording naming economic achievements dates from the 1973 amendment (BGBl. Nr. 394/1973), as the RIS note on the 1985 text shows; the Citizenship Act 1985 carried it as § 10(4) from 31 July 1985; today it is § 10(6) and no longer lists fields. Under METHODOLOGY decision 14 this general special-interest clause is the legal basis, not a launch, and no stored official text makes investing the route, so launched stays empty (the exact 1965 date was not read: the historical Federal Law Gazette archive is behind a bot check). Status active: the provision is in force (aut-ris-stbg-s10-2026).

Residence permit for high net worth investors: ANG 500,000 gives a 3-year permit, ANG 750,000 a 5-year permit and ANG 1,500,000 an indefinite permit; purpose includes purchase of real property or a business investment. The 2014 decree (in force 1 Oct 2014) replaced a Ministerial Decree of 3 August 2009 (not read), so an investor scheme existed earlier; 'launched' left empty. Curaçao is a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; Dutch citizenship after residence is not part of this decree. Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the Immigration Service's current page (last modified 29 September 2026) describes the permit with the same tiers now in XCG (500,000 / 750,000 / 1,500,000; fees XCG 1,865 / 3,095 / 6,170) and takes applications online. A 2025 revamp reported in the press was not found on the official page. The 2009 decree predates Curaçao becoming a country within the Kingdom (2010); it was not read, so launched stays empty. No counts found.

Residence for a foreigner making a long-term, non-speculative investment of at least EUR 10 million in commercial or industrial assets in France, as listed in comparison tables by the UK Migration Advisory Committee (Feb 2014; residence requirement 183 days a year) and the IMF (2015 working paper and Vanuatu Article IV; inception year 2013). Neither table names the card; the name comes from Transparency International's 2018 report, which cites Decree No 2009-1114 of 11 September 2009 on the carte de résident for an exceptional economic contribution and dates a French residence-by-investment scheme to 2009 (amended 2016), but its table row describes the EUR 300,000 passeport talent (fra-passeport-talent-investor), so that 2009 date is not recorded as a launch event. launched follows the IMF table (2013); the decree and the law behind the card are not stored, and the two dates disagree. The 5-year citizenship qualifying period in the MAC and IMF tables is France's ordinary naturalisation period and is kept as a context row without a programme. Status left blank (checked 2026-10-11): the current CESEDA (consolidated to 27 August 2026, read from a reproduction because Légifrance blocks automated access) contains no residence card for an exceptional economic contribution, so the card appears to have been removed, but the repealing act was not found. Counts not found.

Investor residence for foreigners who invest capital in any lawful economic activity, or in state or national financial-institution securities and bonds; investor status certified by MIFIC, requirements set by regulation (Decreto 31-2012, not read). Investor residents who have set up an industry or activity contributing to development may naturalise after two years of permanent residence. No amount in the law; press and industry cite USD 30,000 (not confirmed from an official text). Launched 1993-05-30: Ley 153 (La Gaceta 80 of 30 April 1993), which creates the 'inmigrante con capital' category, comes into force 30 days after publication (date computed); it repealed Decreto 1031 of 1982, which was not read. Ley 761 (in force August 2011) continues the category. A DGME news item of April 2019 lists the documents for investor residence (including MIFIC's investment registration certificate) and reports rising applications, so the route operated in 2019; status is left blank because no current official page could be read (the DGME site returns HTTP 403). In scope under decision 15 (refined): the law leaves the amount to regulation, so the investment rule is recorded with the amount unset.

Residence for foreigners investing in reforestation or forest plantations authorised by the National Environment Authority, personally or through a company (at most two foreign applicants per company). DE 320 of 2008 sets two permits: temporary, B/.60,000 on at least 10 hectares, six years renewable every two (arts. 95, 100-102); permanent, B/.80,000 on at least 20 hectares (arts. 180-182); B/.2,000 more per dependant in both. SNM approvals fell from 71 in 2010 to 2 in 2020 and none in 2021; the category does not appear separately in the 2022-2026 tables. The OECD listed a Panama 'Reforestation Investor Visa' as potentially high-risk for tax reporting in October 2018; in its 20 November 2018 version the scheme ('Reforestation Investor Permit') moved to a separate table in which only Panamanian ID cards with reference code 'PRP-FOR' count as potentially high-risk. Launch is the 2008 regulation, the first stored text; the SNM table note says its series also rests on the 1960 migration law. Decreto Ejecutivo 199 of 2021 (in force 20 May 2021) raised the minimums to B/.80,000 (temporary) and B/.100,000 (permanent), dropped the minimum areas, added permanent residence directly for B/.350,000 and a 5-year holding period; the current SNM sheets restate these amounts and charge B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM). Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found.

Temporary residence for foreigners who have invested at least B/.60,000, personally or through a company, in agriculture, livestock or aquaculture in lines the Agriculture Ministry considers of national interest, plus B/.500 per dependant; valid six years, renewable every two (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 95-99). SNM approvals: 35 in 2010-2021 (none above 12 a year), and 3 extensions in 2023. The current SNM sheet restates B/.60,000, B/.500 per dependant and six years, but mentions only personal investment (not through a company); fees B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM). Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found. No amending decree for this category was found in the SNM decree list.

Residence for foreigners who are sole holders of shares worth at least B/.160,000 in a company with a commercial licence (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 185-186). SNM approvals fell to 10-15 a year by 2020-2021; the category no longer appears separately in the 2022-2026 tables. The current SNM sheet restates B/.160,000 per applicant, B/.2,000 per dependant and five Panamanian employees per applicant, and says the first permit is a two-year provisional one; fees B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM). Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found.

Permanent residence for foreigners who invest at least B/.250,000 from abroad in the risk capital of a company of the Panamá-Pacífico special economic area (the former Howard air base) or its developer or operator; the company must be authorised under Ley 41 of 2004 (not stored) and employ at least three Panamanians (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 206-208). The SNM tables have no separate investor row for the area (only employee and technician categories). The current SNM sheet restates B/.250,000 and three Panamanian employees; fees B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM); its legal basis cites DE 320 as amended by DE 26 of 2 March 2009 (not stored). Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found.

Permanent residence for foreigners who invest at least B/.250,000 from abroad in a promoter or operator of an export processing zone or a company in one (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 211-213), referring to the zones law, Ley 25 of 1992 (not stored). SNM approvals ('Inversionista o Empr. de Zonas Procesadoras'): 52 in 2010-2021, at most 16 a year. The current SNM sheet restates B/.250,000 from abroad; fees B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM); legal basis DE 320 as amended by DE 26 of 2009 (not stored). Not shown separately in SNM tables after 2021 (small categories are grouped as other categories from 2024). Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found.

Permanent residence for foreigners investing in a company providing call-centre services for export; DE 320 of 2008 (arts. 214-216) gives it the same requirements as the export processing zone investor permit (B/.250,000 from abroad, art. 211) and says this follows Decreto Ejecutivo 97 of 2002 (not stored), which may itself have created the permit. SNM approvals: 2 in 2013, 81 in 2021, 39 in 2022; not shown separately in 2023-2026. The current SNM sheet repeats art. 214 (same requirements as the processing-zone permit) and charges B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM); it states no amount of its own. Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found.

Permanent residence for foreigners who invest more than B/.150,000 from abroad in the film industry, in a company authorised under the special regime of Ley 36 of 2007 (not stored), certified by the Panama Film Commission (DE 320 of 2008, arts. 217-219); no amount per dependant is set. Fees are the general art. 315 rates for permanent permits for special policies (B/.250 application, B/.100 card). The category has no row in the stored SNM residence tables 2010-2026 (only 'Empleados de Empresas Cinematográficas', staff permits, which are out of scope). The current SNM sheet restates more than B/.150,000 and charges B/.250 (Treasury) plus B/.800 (SNM), which differs from the art. 315 fees above. Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the SNM's current website lists a requirements sheet for this category among residence permits (pan-snm-req-index-2026), and no repeal or suspension was found. No approvals appear in any SNM table, so whether anyone has used it is unknown.

SNM category for businesspeople at the City of Knowledge (Ciudad del Saber), a research and business park run by a foundation under Decreto Ley 6 of 1999. In the 2008 regulation (DE 320, art. 113) the matching subcategory is 'empresario o ejecutivo' of the City of Knowledge Foundation: it needs the Foundation's certificate that the company may operate there and a parent-company letter, and sets no investment amount. Launch is left empty because no stored text makes investing the route; whether the category is in scope under decision 15 needs a second look. SNM approvals: 301 in 2010-2021, 5 extensions in 2023, 48 in 2024. The current SNM sheet for the businessperson or executive of the City of Knowledge Foundation (DE 320 arts. 108, 113-114) asks for the Foundation's authorisation of the company and a parent-company letter, and sets no investment amount and no fee; status active because the SNM lists it as a current category and approved 48 permits in 2024. Launch stays empty and the scope question stands: nothing in the current sheet makes investing the route.

Known only from the SNM statistics: 478 permits approved 2010-2021, 180 of them in 2010, falling to none after 2016 apart from 1 in 2019. No stored document sets its requirements or start: the 2008 migration regulation (DE 320) has no small-business investor section, so the category may come from earlier rules. Status still blank (checked 2026-10-11): the category has no requirements sheet among the SNM's current residence categories (pan-snm-req-index-2026) and no section in DE 320, but no repeal act or official statement closing it was found; the last approval in the stored tables is 1 in 2019.

Provincial nomination route (leading to Canadian permanent residence) for people who invest in Prince Edward Island. According to the UK Migration Advisory Committee (Feb 2014, citing the agent website Investor Visa Canada), it opened in January 2014 with 400 places for 2014 and required net worth of at least C$600,000, management expertise, an investment of C$150,000 in a qualifying business and an intention to live in the province; the MAC adds that no further details were available and that the route resembles an entrepreneur route more than a passive investor route. Archived pages of the PEI Office of Immigration (2014-2016) show the route as the Business Impact Category's 100% Ownership and Partial Ownership streams: net worth C$600,000, an investment of C$150,000 in a PEI business the applicant actively manages (for Partial Ownership, at least one third of the voting shares, or alternatively an investment of at least C$1 million) and a C$200,000 escrow deposit refunded in stages; a third stream (Work Permit) required the applicant to come on a work permit first and is not part of this programme. Closed: PEI announced that after 20 September 2018 it would invite only Work Permit stream entrepreneurs, as the 100% Ownership and Partial Ownership streams would close; ended is set to that date (the last day invitations could be issued under them). Whether January 2014 was the streams' first opening is still not confirmed (PEI's business immigration streams are older; earlier versions not read). No counts found: the stored IRCC provincial nominee tables give Prince Edward Island totals for all nominee streams together, and the 2014 CIC evaluation's Prince Edward Island figures concern the federal Immigrant Investor Program (can-iip).

Permit for owners of a home worth at least US$300,000 (reg 33(3)), valid 5 years (reg 34(2)), fee US$1,500 (Schedule 7). Separate from the investor residence permit (reg 24, condition B). The current Ordinance and Regulations came into force on 1 April 2016; the Ordinance repealed and re-enacted an earlier one, which was not read, so the launch is left empty. Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the Border Control website lists Home Owners among the residence permit categories it issues, its FAQ gives a processing time of up to six weeks for the Home Owner category, the current application form has a Home Owner box, and no repeal or suspension was found. No counts found.

The Law on Immigration (No. 2491-III, adopted 7 June 2001) lists, among the categories that may receive an immigration permit (permanent residence) within the yearly immigration quota, persons who made a foreign investment in Ukraine's economy in convertible currency of at least USD 100,000. The clause is in the first edition and in the current text (reworded in 2016 and 2023). Launched = entry into force 07.08.2001 per the Rada's document card (the law enters into force one month after publication; first published 07.07.2001). Until 2023 the Cabinet set a yearly immigration quota; the quota orders for 2022 and 2023 put no limit on the investor category ("без обмеження"), and none has been issued for 2024-2026. Since Law 3180-IX (in force 20 October 2023) a quota is set only in case of mass arrival. Status active (checked 2026-10-11): the investor clause is in the current law and no act suspending immigration permits under martial law was found; the number of permits granted to investors was not found.

The current SNM sheet (empresario o ejecutivo, DE 320 arts. 108, 113-114) sets no investment amount, so whether the category is in scope under decision 15 still needs a decision; status set active because it is a current category with 48 approvals in 2024.

Panama: SNM tables from 2024 group small categories as 'Otras categorías', so approvals for agrarian, forestry, macro, processing-zone and call-centre investors after 2023 cannot be read; status rests on the current requirement sheets instead.

The exact date of the 1965 Act and of the 1973 amendment could not be read: the ONB historical Federal Law Gazette (ALEX) is behind a Cloudflare check.
